title: The brothers come for grain (Genesis 42–44)
hookLine: Joseph tests them, and Judah offers himself for Benjamin

lines: TEN BROTHERS GO DOWN TO EGYPT.
THEY BOW, AND DON'T KNOW HIM.
cards: The famine reaches Canaan. Old Jacob hears there's grain in Egypt and sends ten of his sons to buy some. Not the youngest, Benjamin, Rachel's last son; Jacob won't risk him.
The ten bow, faces to the ground, before the governor of Egypt, with no idea who he is: an Egyptian name, Egyptian clothes, an interpreter between them.
He knows them at once, and remembers the dreams: sheaves bowing down to his. What would you do with your brothers in that room?

teach.h: SPIES! THEY CONFESS THEIR OLD GUILT.
teach.b: Joseph doesn't reveal himself. He tests them. First, he calls them spies and holds them three days.
Then he keeps one brother, Simeon, and sends the rest home: bring your youngest back, and I'll believe you.

In front of him, thinking he can't understand, they talk in their own language: we are guilty about our brother; we saw his distress when he begged us, and we wouldn't listen. Joseph turns aside and weeps.
Second, the hard road home. Jacob refuses to send Benjamin.

teach.h: JUDAH PLEDGES HIMSELF FOR THE BOY.
teach.b: Only when the grain runs out does Judah speak up: put the boy in my hands, and if I don't bring him back, let me bear the blame forever. Third, the trap.

teach.h: A SILVER CUP IN BENJAMIN'S SACK.
teach.b: In Egypt, a feast, then a silver cup hidden in Benjamin's sack. The steward finds it, and the governor's verdict is simple: the one with the cup becomes my slave; the rest of you can go home.
They've stood at this door before: years ago they let Rachel's son be carried off to Egypt and went home without him. They could do it again, and legally. Fourth, Judah steps forward.
He tells the whole story, the old father, the lost son, how the father's life is bound up in the boy's, and then he asks: let me stay as your slave instead; let the boy go home.

This is the same Judah who once said sell him for silver. Matthew's Gospel traces Jesus's family through him. Look back over the week: a wrestler renamed Israel, Esau running, the coat, the pit, the prison, the dreams.
A family that kept breaking, and now someone stands in the gap.

how: Some Catholic preaching sees in Judah's offer to take Benjamin's place a picture of Christ, whom the Book of the Apocalypse calls the lion of the tribe of Juda.

games.q: what does “the brothers come for grain” mean?
o: Jacob's sons going home to bury their father
the brothers' trip to Egypt, and Joseph's test
the seven fat years when Egypt stored food

games.q: who did what in Egypt — tap the pairs.
p: kept in Egypt as a hostage
Rachel's last son, kept at home
offered to be a slave in his place

s: the brothers recognized Joseph when they first bowed
they had no idea. he knew them at once, and spoke through an interpreter.
Judah offered to stay as a slave so Benjamin could go home
the same Judah who once had the idea of selling Joseph.
Joseph wept when he heard his brothers confess their guilt
they talked among themselves, not knowing he understood, and he turned aside and wept.

games.q: you're one of the brothers. the governor found his cup in Benjamin's sack. he says the boy stays as a slave and the rest of you can go home in peace. what do you do?
o: go home. it's legal, and it's not your fault.
offer yourself as a slave in the boy's place.
games.why: Judah steps forward, tells the whole story of the old father and the lost son, and asks to stay instead of Benjamin. the brothers who once sold Rachel's son won't leave this one.

practice: Think of someone carrying something heavy right now: a coworker buried in a deadline, a parent with a sick kid, a friend facing a hard phone call. Picture taking their place for an hour, a covered shift, a seat in the waiting room.
If you pray, hold that person before God, the way Judah held his brother before the governor; if you don't, keep them in mind for a minute.

wordCard.voice: The brothers come for grain. Hungry, guilty and bowing, they're tested, until Judah offers himself in Benjamin's place. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: grain for sale, the word Jacob uses when he hears there's grain in Egypt (Genesis 42:1–2).

carryVoice: Your line: judah stepped forward. This time, one brother stands in for another. Until tomorrow.
